findings.message: This round adds `drafted_by` (the pusher's actor id) to `delivery.commit_day_draft`. That is a personal `*_by` column, but `module.ts` `retention` has no entry for `delivery.commit_day_draft`. `scripts/check-module-standard.mjs` fails the module for this, and 032 erasure and legal holds will never find the pusher named in these rows. Fix: add a retention entry with `subject: ["drafted_by", "user_id"]`, `fields: ["drafted_by"]`, a period and an action, in line with `delivery.sync_push`.
findings.rule: docs/module-standard.md (personal data has a retention rule)
findings.scenario: Person P pushes and drafts a day, then an erasure request for P is completed → P's id stays in commit_day_draft.drafted_by, which no retention rule lists; the module-standard check also fails on the new `*_by` column.

findings.message: The consent fix only covers the sync. The webhook path (`ingestPush` → `draftCommitTime`) still asks only `commitTimeOn`: is it on now? It never checks the commit against the start of the current enabled period from `commitTimeSince`. So the 'one consent rule' is applied two ways: the sync drops commits made while commit time was off, and the webhook drafts them. Fix: in `draftCommitTime`, refuse a commit whose instant is before `commitTimeSince(...).get(userId)`. Pass the commit's timestamp, not only `day`.
findings.scenario: An Admin switches commit time off on Nov 1 and on again on Nov 10. A branch with a Nov 5 commit carrying `Time: 2h` is pushed on Nov 11 → the webhook drafts 2 h for Nov 5. The sync would leave the same commit out.

findings.message: Two day rules now meet in one dedupe. The sync keys `commit_day_draft.day` on the author's entity-zone day (`dayIn(person.zone)`). The webhook passes `day = c.at.slice(0, 10)` (ingest.ts:63), which is UTC or the git-local offset. The new `commit_day_draft` check in `draftCommitTime` compares the two, so it misses whenever they differ. The Time suggestion also lands on a different day than the sync's for the same work. Fix: make the webhook derive `day` from the commit instant through the same `dayIn(entityZone)` rule, and test it across zones.
findings.scenario: A Colombo author makes commit X at 2026-11-08T20:00Z with a `Time: 1h` line, and commit Y in the same session without one. The sync first drafts the day 2026-11-09 and claims X and Y. A later webhook commit Z, also at 20:10Z on that session, arrives with day '2026-11-08' → the day check misses and Z drafts 1 h on Nov 8. The same evening is counted twice.

findings.message: The cross-path claim is check-then-act. The sync reads `commit_draft` (`alreadyDrafted`) before it estimates. Later it inserts the commit ids with `on conflict do nothing` and ignores whether each insert won. A concurrent webhook that claimed the same commit in between keeps its draft, and the sync's day draft still counts that commit. The README now promises that 'a later `Time:` line can't draft them again', but no test runs two real concurrent sessions. Fix: claim the commit ids first, using `returning` to see which inserts won, and estimate only from the claimed ids. Add a two-session race test that fails without the claim.
findings.scenario: The webhook (Time: 1.5h on commit X) and a CI sync carrying X run concurrently. The sync's alreadyDrafted sees nothing, then the webhook commits its commit_draft row, then the sync's insert of X silently conflicts → X is counted both in the 1.5 h webhook suggestion and in the sync's day estimate.

findings.message: `foldsCommits` reads any second change mention as a squash, so the fix catches only GitHub's default body list and gets other cases wrong both ways. (1) False positive: an ordinary work commit whose body names another change is dropped. The test now asserts `true` for that case, and commit `b` in commits-104.test.ts was rewritten so it no longer mentions `specclaw(102-other)`, which hides the regression. (2) False negative: a squash made with GitHub's 'Default to pull request title' setting, or with a hand-edited message, has one subject line and no body list. It is still counted as fresh work on the merge day. Fix: count only lines that start with a change subject (`^\s*[*-]?\s*specclaw\(`), not mentions anywhere. Also detect a squash by the merge itself, for example a commit on the default branch whose author date equals its committer date and which `git cherry`/patch-id matches branch commits, or the `(#NNN)` PR suffix. Test both variants.
findings.scenario: (1) 'specclaw(101-export): T3\n\nfollows specclaw(099-auth)' → the commit is dropped and that day's hours are never drafted. (2) A squash with subject 'specclaw(101-export): export (#120)' and an empty body, merged on Nov 14 for work done Nov 10–12 → 0.5 h is drafted on Nov 14.

findings.message: A service credential (CI) is trusted to draft for every author, but the author email it sends is git's self-asserted `user.email`, which nobody verified. Matching it to a verified `git_identity` email proves only that the colleague owns the address, not that the colleague wrote the commit. So the previous finding's attack still works through CI: anyone whose commit reaches the synced branch drafts hours in a colleague's name. The draft also claims that person's `commit_day_draft` day, which blocks the colleague's real commits that arrive later for that day. Fix: for CI, attribute only commits the provider verified (signed or provider-verified author), or don't let an unverified draft claim the day.
findings.scenario: Engineer A runs `git commit --author='Nimal <nimal@lumenlabs.test>' -m 'specclaw(101-export): x'` and the commit merges. CI syncs → a 0.5 h suggestion is drafted for Nimal, audited as Nimal's, and Nimal's FLT-101 day is claimed.

findings.message: The consent-period fix (`notified_at` resets on off→on and is kept on on→on) ships with no test. No test drives `setCommitTimeLogging` through on → off → on and checks that commits from the off period don't draft, while a repeated 'on' keeps the period. The sync tests set consent by hand with `db.consent()`, which upserts `notified_at` directly, so they stay green with the CASE expression reverted. Fix: add a table-driven test through the real service over at least these variants: off→on, on→on, on→off→on.
findings.scenario: Revert the CASE to the old `coalesce(...)` → every existing test still passes.

findings.message: Two rules now decide which commits belong to a day, and they disagree. `estimateDays` gives each day every commit of any session that touches it (estimate.ts:56). `daysFor` builds `ids` from commits whose own timestamp falls on that day. So `commit_day_draft.commits` and the audit `commits` disagree with `commit_ids` in the same row. The suggestion says 'From N commits' on each day, so N is counted twice across the days. A day reached only by the 30-minute lead-in gets a draft with `commit_ids: []`. The traceability promised by the B5 fix does not hold. Fix: take the count and the ids from the same per-day set, ideally returned by estimateDays.
findings.scenario: Asia/Colombo, commits at 18:15Z and 18:45Z on Nov 12, which are 23:45 and 00:15 local. Rows: Nov 12 {commits: 2, commit_ids: [c1]} and Nov 13 {commits: 2, commit_ids: [c2]}. Two suggestions each read 'From 2 commits', four in total for two commits.

findings.message: `drafted_by` records `ctx.actor.id` only. For an agent pushing over MCP for a person, `onBehalfOf` is lost, so the row doesn't say whose push it was, even though `mayDraftFor` decided by that person. Record `onBehalfOf` as well.
findings.scenario: Claude pushes for Nimal → drafted_by = 'agent:…', with no Nimal on the row.

findings.message: `SCAN_WEEKS = 52` still caps the scan before the approver filter. A week waiting for this approver that is older than the 52 newest submitted weeks drops off the list silently, and nothing says the scan was cut short. The list also runs one `teamWeek` per scanned week, up to 52 per Overview load. Either page until 8 approvable weeks are found, or say the list is incomplete.
findings.scenario: 60 distinct newer weeks are submitted to other approvers → this PM's waiting week does not appear, and nothing indicates it.

findings.message: The popover is positioned once, with `position: fixed` from `getBoundingClientRect()`, and is not repositioned on scroll or resize. When the page scrolls with it open (hover or click), it detaches from its icon. `popover="auto"` opened on hover also light-dismisses any other open auto popover. Reposition it on scroll and resize, or use CSS anchor positioning, and consider `popover="hint"`/manual for the hover case.
findings.scenario: Open the info popover, then scroll the Proposals page → the popover stays fixed in the viewport, away from the icon.
